answer: The forge mints an identity from a sonnet, and it mints one at a time, in filing order. A sonnet must stand thirty epochs of its maker's counted work before the press takes it, and the forge locks one violet of market currency for every sonnet a maker has waiting, releasing it only when that sonnet is minted. An honest newcomer pays the first price, thirty epochs and one violet; an operator's thousandth identity waits behind its own nine hundred and ninety-nine, so its maker locks a thousand violets and waits a thousand epochs for the press to reach it.
